gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.
The twins are ___ over six feet tall.
gaps.explanation: 'Both' is used for exactly two; 'all' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
We went to the exhibition, but there was ___ worth seeing.
gaps.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast, so 'nothing worth seeing' fits the disappointment.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: ___ John and his brother are doctors.
gaps.explanation: 'Both John and his brother are ...' links two people affirmatively; 'neither' and 'either' pair with 'nor/or'.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
